newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says Australian rate cuts to be felt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says Australian rate cuts to be felt.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday that the effect of past Australian rate cuts had yet to be really felt in the economy.
"The impact of falling interest rates has yet to be really felt," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp television.
Pressed on whether the Reserve Bank of Australia might ease monetary policy for a fifth time since July, Howard said the bank had shown good judgement in the past.
"And I believe they will get the next cut or non-movement right as well," he added, without elaborating.
"The benefits of the interest rate cuts will be most strongly felt, and therefore the benefits enjoyed, next year," he said later.
The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy in July, November, December and May, each time dropping its overnight cash rate target by 0.5 percentage points.
It now targets overnight cash at 5.5 percent.

Earlier on Thursday the Australian Bureau of Statistics said its estimate of employment had fallen 40,300 in May from the previous month, prompting economists to say that the economy was weaker than thought and a fifth rate cut more likely.
